newsitem.title: USA: Private Florida orange estimate said 253 mln boxes.
newsitem.headline: Private Florida orange estimate said 253 mln boxes.

text.p: Citrus market sources said a widely watched private industry estimate of Florida's 1997/98 orange crop had come in at 253.0 million 90-pound boxes, well above market expectations.

The estimate, by Florida-based Citrus Consulting Internatinal, was issued privately to the company's clients. The firm declined to confirm or deny the 253.0 million box estimate, which analysts said circulated this morning.
"We do not comment on our estimates," a spokeswoman for the firm told Reuters.

Talk of the higher than expected estimate for production pushed down NYCE orange juice futures sharply on Thursday morning. At 1140 EDT, September FCOJ was down 8.30 cents a lb at 70.95 and November futures onward were locked down the 5.00-cent a lb daily trading limit.
"Anything over 245.0 would have been shocking," one NYCE FCOJ broker said. "We were all surprised by this number."

Florida produced 225.7 million boxes in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) year, out of a total U.S. production of 299.1 million boxes. The Department will issue its first estimate of Florida's 1997/98 crop in October.
Florida produced 203.2 million boxes in 1995/96, out of a total U.S. orange crop of 271.8 million boxes, according to U.S. Agriculture Department figures.
